## 3. Verified source record

The complete JSON entry below is copied from the current local source. Preserve its id, author_id, author_name, day, hour, knowledge_key, timestamp, and exact text. Candidate prose is editorial material, not part of the loaded row.

```json
{
  "id": "journal_raw_b3_13_general_the_vote",
  "text": "The vote was not unanimous. I want to write that down because I do not want to forget it and I do not want to pretend it was easy. Six for, one against, two abstentions. The Electrician voted against. He said he was not voting against children. He said he was voting for the generator. He is right. The generator is the thing that keeps the children in this bunker alive, and the generator runs on fuel, and the fuel is at 15 days, and 15 days is the number I see when I close my eyes. The Surgeon abstained. The Architect abstained. They could not rank the three and they chose not to pretend. That is honest. I respect honest more than I respect agreement. The Therapist watched me during the vote. She has a session with me on Day 172. I think she was watching to see if I would carry it. I will carry it. That is what a general is for. A general is the person who decides and then does not get to put the decision down. The Courier said: if we go, I will go. If we do not go, I will listen for them until the radio stops. He is 22 years old. He should not have to say that. No one should have to say that. But he said it, and he meant it, and the room was quiet after he said it, and the quiet was the thing that decided. Not me. The quiet. I gave the order. The team leaves Day 167. The Courier, the Hunter, the Plumber, the Quartermaster. Four people and 80 litres of water and 56 kilometres of walking and a well that is dry. The Priest said a prayer after the vote. No one joined him. He said it anyway. I did not bow my head. I am not a man who bows his head. But I heard it. I heard all of it. The prayer was not for Kilo. The prayer was for us. I think the Priest knows that. I think the Priest has known that since the chapel emptied. I will address the bunker on Day 171 when the team is back. I do not know what I will say. I know what I will not say. I will not say it was the right decision. I do not know if it was the right decision. I know it was the decision. That is all a general gets to know.",
  "timestamp": "Day 165, 23h",
  "author_name": "The General",
  "author_id": "the_general",
  "knowledge_key": "the_kilo_vote_non_unanimous",
  "day": 165,
  "hour": 23.0
}
```

## 4. Fixed canon and open space

The vote is six for, one against, and two abstentions. The Electrician votes against for the generator; the Surgeon and Architect abstain. The General orders a four-person team to leave on Day 167 for a dry well, with 80 litres of water and 56 kilometres of walking. The General says he does not know whether it was the right decision. Do not add a later result to this pre-departure entry. Candidate language may add an image, rhythm, or private impression as an editorial draft, but no proposed addition becomes a further remembered event or a confirmed fact until the existing content owner selects and reviews it against the source.

## 5. Human center

The source voice is The General. The General’s account is disciplined, self-questioning, and explicit about dissent. Keep the vote count, the Electrician’s reason, the abstentions, and the Courier’s offer; do not turn the mission order into unanimous consent. The prose may notice what the author can count, hear, repair, fear, or leave uncertain, while keeping the account’s limits visible.
